verdict: Caution on Panipat home textiles: lend selectively to organised towel/bedsheet converters with diversified buyers and recycled-yarn integration; avoid blanket-only units exposed to the 50% domestic demand collapse [1][2].
title: Panipat home textiles & made-ups: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
Panipat turns waste cloth into yarn and then into blankets, rugs, towels and bedsheets — roughly 50 containers of used clothes arrive daily and are recycled into yarn [3]. Cash comes from converting cheap fibre into finished home textiles sold to domestic wholesale and export buyers. **Value sits in the spinning-to-finishing chain and in buyer relationships, not in the loom.** Capital is fixed-heavy (power looms, spinning, finishing) and working capital is inventory-led, with receivables stretching the cycle further [10][11]. So when a proposal lands, check how much of the unit is actually spinning and finishing versus plain weaving; if it is only weaving, ask who owns the yarn and on what credit. ## What has broken now
Local reporting says the blanket industry faces a nearly 50% decline in domestic demand this season, on top of an overseas slowdown tied to the Iran-Israel-US conflict [1][2]. **That is a blanket-specific shock, not a towel/bedsheet shock.** Peer results point the other way: Welspun Living Q2 FY27 revenue rose 16.9% to Rs 2,870 crore with home textile exports up 18.3% and domestic business up 28.2% [6]; Indo Count posted record Q1 FY27 revenue of Rs 1,224 crore at 13.1% EBITDA margin [7]. Note the ANI piece is about 10 months old [3]. **So when a blanket-only proposal lands, ask for the last six months of order book and buyer-wise sales; if domestic wholesale is the bulk, decline or cut exposure.**

## Where the growth is
Haryana GST collections rose 10.1% Apr-to-date versus India's 6.1% [D], and India-wide textile output (NIC 13) grew 13.1% YoY to Aug-2026 [D]. **Pursue organised towel and bedsheet converters with export or branded-domestic buyers, and units integrated into recycled-yarn spinning.** Peer evidence supports this: Welspun's global B2B innovation products grew 16% and other B2B 32% [4], and Iris Clothings grew total income 40.3% YoY in Q2 FY27 [5]. Avoid blanket-only units selling to domestic wholesale [1][2]. ## How to grow safely
Structure as cash credit plus a term loan matched to the spinning/finishing capex, not to loom additions. **Take monthly stock-and-receivable statements, buyer-wise sales, and a quarterly CMA; covenant on total outside liabilities to tangible net worth and interest cover.** Rating reports show conservative peers running gearing of 0.6 times and TOL/TNW of 0.9 times [8]; use that as the benchmark, and collect from customer where their own numbers are missing. - Buyer-wise sales (monthly): top buyer share above half -> seek diversification or reduce limit. - GST returns (monthly): turnover falling two quarters running -> reassess limit. - Power and yarn purchase bills (monthly): output falling with no order-book reason -> shift to watch list.
